subject: ventures/cabinet-refinishing-bid-calculator
professional: an estimator at a cabinet-refinishing or painting shop (PCA-style production estimator) who bids kitchens by piece count and checks labor hours, material gallons and margin. First check: does the margin math hold, are drawer fronts and frames counted the way shops count them, and does a dark-to-light job add the paint it really consumes.

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the venture dir: 120 tests, 120 pass. Recomputed by hand in Python (not calc.mjs) with the real index.html defaults (wage 38, burden 30, primer 48/gal @22, finish 68/gal @18, supplies 85, travel 275, overhead 15, margin 25). (1) 10 doors/8 drawers/9 openings shop spray: pieces 10+8+9*0.6=23.4, hours 13.5+6+5.85+3.42+4=32.77, loaded wage 49.40, labor 1618.84, 2+2 gallons, materials 317, cost 2542.46, price cost/0.75 = 3389.95, $339.00/door, $125.55/piece: all match calc.mjs and the README. (2) same kitchen on-site brush (factor 1.55 on doors/drawers/openings only): 46.7125 h, price 4446.05, matches README. (3) 20/16/18 dark-to-light: 70.46 h (36 removable * 0.22 extra coat), 3+3 gallons, price 6422.71, matches. Margin identity price=cost/(1-m) is the correct markup-vs-margin treatment. Independent coverage check: typical label ~350 sq ft/gal; a door ~15x30in is about 7 sq ft both sides plus edges, so 27 pieces need ~0.9 gal finish (2 coats) and ~0.5 gal primer. The tool's 18 and 22 pieces/gal give 2 gal each after Math.ceil: conservative (accounts for spray transfer loss), not wrong, but the rate is unsourced. Did not verify the hours-per-door defaults against a published labor standard; none cited.
evidence.completeness: Checked in a real Chrome (playwright-core) over http://localhost: preset buttons render, applying one fills 10/8/9 and shows 32.8 h and '2 primer + 2 finish'; all four pages (index, vs-kickserv, vs-a-flat-price-per-door, SEO article) load with 0 pageerrors. Printable proposal, share link, usage counter, summary copy exist and have tests. FAILED: README says 'Open index.html directly in a browser'; loaded via file:// the preset list is empty and the price stays '$-' (the page's script does not run from file://, module import is blocked), so the headline run instruction is untrue. Not done: VENTURE.yaml stage is prototype, all 3 hypotheses untested, no usage data. README limitation admits islands/vanities and a single blended wage are not modelled. No TODO/stubs in calc.mjs.
evidence.verification: 120 tests pass. Seeded three mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted from a saved copy (git status clean afterwards): M1 `removablePieces = doors + drawers` -> `doors` (extra coat ignores drawer fronts): CAUGHT (2 failures). M2 `/(1 - targetMargin/100)` -> `/(1 + targetMargin/100)`: CAUGHT (4 failures). M3 Math.ceil -> Math.floor in gallonCount: CAUGHT (4 failures). Also page.test.mjs guards against the unclosed-raw-text-element class of page defect. Gap: no test loads the page in a browser, which is why the file:// failure and any DOM wiring bug would not be caught.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (308 lines) fully and skimmed index.html. Pure functions, input validation with named errors, JSDoc, no dependencies, margin >= 100 rejected, divide-by-zero guarded. Defects: opening weight 0.6 is hardcoded in pieceEquivalent's default and not exposed; the extra coat adds labor hours but no finish gallons (see domain); `costShare`/proposed.margin guard cases fine; the browser UI re-implements field lists in a 714-line single HTML file; no unit handling beyond USD.
evidence.claims: Checked: README worked example ($3,389.95, $339.00, $125.55, 32.77 h, walk-away $2,542.46, brush $4,446.05) all reproduce exactly. Disclaimer and no-warranty text present on README and pages; privacy claim (no network, localStorage tally only) is consistent with usage.mjs and the page having no fetch. vs-kickserv.html is careful: states Kickserv founded 2006 and category only, admits its site was not reachable, gives no Kickserv prices, non-affiliation notice; I could not confirm the 2006 date or feature list independently from this sandbox, so the claim is unverified but low-risk. Unbacked: 'Open index.html directly in a browser' is false (file:// does not work). Starting hours and coverage are described as ballpark, which is honest, but no source is given for any default.
evidence.fitness: Walked a painter's job: pick the 10/8 galley preset, switch to brush and dark-to-light, enter a customer's counter-price, read margin and walk-away, print a proposal. Works over http and on the hosted URL pattern. A real shop would then hit: no per-room or island/vanity split, one blended wage (sprayer vs helper), no sqft or door-size input so large slab doors and small shaker doors cost the same, no tax or deposit-by-percent beyond the proposal terms, and defaults the user must replace themselves. Usable for a quick sanity bid, not a replacement for a shop's own labor data.
evidence.domain: Compared with how refinishing shops estimate (piece count by doors, drawer fronts, then frame/box linear feet or sqft; separate prep, prime, 2 finish coats; materials by coverage). Departures: (1) face-frame openings counted as a piece (0.6 weight) rather than by linear feet or sqft of frame and box, crude for boxes, end panels, crown and toe kick, none of which are priced; (2) dark-to-light adds 0.22 h per removable piece but no extra gallons of finish or primer, so material is understated on exactly the jobs the product highlights; (3) extra coat never applies to frames or openings; (4) degrease is a manual hour entry, not scaled to job size; (5) hardware hours count hinges and pulls together at one rate. Margin-on-price vs markup is handled correctly, and burden/overhead separation is sound practice.

defects.what: README says to open index.html directly; over file:// the page script does not run (no presets, price stays a dash).
Dark-to-light adds extra-coat labor but no extra finish or primer gallons, understating material on the headline use case.
Opening weight 0.6 is a hidden constant; extra coat excludes openings; coverage and hours defaults carry no source.
No browser-level test; tests would not catch the file:// failure.

verdict: The arithmetic is right: three scenarios recomputed by hand match to the cent, the margin math is correct, and three seeded mutations were all caught by the 120 passing tests. It falls short of the bar on claims (the README's 'open index.html directly' instruction fails in a real browser) and on domain depth: material is not scaled for the extra coat, frames and boxes are a crude piece weight, and no default hours or coverage cites a source. The Kickserv comparison page is honest and avoids unverified facts. Correctness, verification and claims-minus-one-defect are near 3; claims is scored 2 for the false run instruction, so it does not meet the bar. It is finished enough to use over http but is a tested prototype by its own VENTURE.yaml stage.
